**Done before:** Nothing builds a `Template` class or a `Property` class yet. The closest work is the paging templates ([2026-09-05 paging-templates](/framework/ai/2026-09-05/paging-templates/)), which are plain modules under `public/imagine/paging/templates/` (`families.js`, `page.js`, and folders for magazine, blog, screens, shells). Page body parts landed today ([2026-10-12 page-slice](/framework/ai/2026-10-12/page-slice/)), with `core/Page/parts/` holding `Part.js`, `Parts.js`, `CardPart.js` and `TextPart.js`.

**Still live?** Yes for both. `public/imagine/paging/templates/` exists and the parts classes are in `core/Page/parts/`. A Grep for `class Template`, `class Property` and `bindProperty` finds no code, only the brief that asks for them.

**Same or different:** The ask is different. The paging templates are data-driven families, not a `Page` subclass, and nothing binds a property to a live value. The new ask overlaps with `core/Page/parts/` only in that parts are streamed from a page's `page.jsonl`, so a template's bound fields could feed the same parts. I did not check whether `Item`'s event system already covers what the owner wants from `Property`.

**Advice:** Extend `core/Page` for the `Template` class, and reuse the parts classes for what it renders. Build `Property` as its own small class and check it against `Item`'s events before writing it, so there is one event system. The brief is at [page-templates requirements.md](/framework/ai/sessions/2026/10/12/session-87bec773/page-templates/requirements.md). No files written.

**Done before:** A full sortable, resizable grid already exists: [ext/DataGrid](/framework/ext/DataGrid/) (2026-10-03 task, landed). It does resize, sort, filters, windowing past 300 rows, and table or card views. The markup it's built on came from [ui/datagrid](/framework/ui/datagrid/), which now re-exports it.

**Still live?** Yes. `DataGrid.js` exists and `ui/table`, `ui/datagrid` and the audit pages import it. The Sessions list is not on it. [ai/sessions](/framework/ai/sessions/) has no import of DataGrid; it uses its own CSS grid (`sessions.css`), built in [sessions-grid-v2](/framework/ai/2026-10-02/sessions-grid-v2/). That is a hand-built grid, not the shared one.

**Same or different:** The ask is the same thing DataGrid already does. What's different is only the sessions list, which has its own grid and has not been moved to the shared one. I did not open the sessions-grid-v2 outcome in full, so I have not confirmed whether it has resize or sort.

**Advice:** Extend, don't build new. Point the sessions list at `DataGrid` with `columns` for Start, Source, Name, Model, State and Cost, and pass `href(row)` to link each row to its session. Remove the sessions-only grid CSS afterwards. This follows the one-of-everything rule. Check first that the sessions page doesn't need features DataGrid lacks.

**Notes:** I opened 2 readmes and one task listing, and ran 3 greps. I wrote no files.
